qualification.reason: The document is a Request for Proposals (RFP) issued by the City/County Association of Governments of San Mateo County for a planning project, including submission deadlines, scope of work, and evaluation criteria.

quotes.quote:
REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS 
 San Mateo Countywide Safe Streets for All Supplemental Planning 
Project
Proposals are due: January 23, 2026, 12:00PM PST

The City/County Association of Governments of San Mateo County (C/CAG), a Joint Powers Agency composed of the County of San Mateo and all twenty cities located within San Mateo County, invites qualified consultants to submit proposals for San Mateo Countywide Safe Streets for All Supplemental Planning Project, which is funded through the U.S. Department of Transportation (USDOT) Safe Streets for All (SS4A) Grant Program.

findings.title: Project Examples: Minimum Three Projects in Past Five Years
findings.fact: Proposals must include detailed descriptions of at least three projects completed within the past five years, including contracting agency, project manager, contact info, contract amount, funding source, dates, and outcomes.

quotes.quote: Demonstrate successful completion of comparable projects. These projects must illustrate the quality, type, and past performance of the project team. Include a detailed description of a minimum of three projects within the past five years, with the following information:

findings.title: References: Three to Five References
findings.fact: Proposals must provide three to five references for work completed within five years of the RFP issuance, with accessible contact information.

quotes.quote: Provide three to five references (no more than five including references for subcontractors) and their contact information. References should be for work completed within five years of the date of the issuance of this RFP, and the contact person must be currently accessible via the contact information provided to be considered.

findings.title: Mandatory Certifications
findings.fact: No mandatory certifications such as ISO or CMMI are required, but federal certifications and forms are required.

quotes.quote: Proposals must contain the following federal certifications or forms: (1) Certification Regarding Lobbying, (2) Certification Regarding Debarment, Suspension, Ineligibility, and Voluntary Exclusion—Lower Tier Covered Transactions, and (3) Disclosure of Lobbying Activities (SF-LLL) form.

findings.title: Protest Deadline for RFP Provisions
findings.fact: Objections to RFP provisions must be submitted no later than 5:00 p.m. on the third business day prior to the date Responses to RFP are due.

quotes.quote: No later than 5:00 p.m. on the third business day prior to the date Responses to RFP are due, for objections to RFP provisions.

findings.title: Protest Deadline for Non-Responsive Determination
findings.fact: Protests regarding non-responsive determination must be submitted no later than 5:00 p.m. on the third business day after the date the proposer is notified.

quotes.quote: No later than 5:00 p.m. on the third business day after the date the proposer is notified that it did not meet the minimum qualifications or was found to be non-responsive.

findings.title: Protest Deadline for Award Recommendation
findings.fact: Protests regarding award recommendation must be submitted no later than 5:00 p.m. on the third business day after the date the proposer is notified that it was not selected, or if applicable, the date the Committee recommends award, whichever is later.

quotes.quote: No later than 5:00 p.m. on the third business day after the date on which the proposer is notified that it was not selected, or, if applicable, the date the Committee recommends award, whichever is later, for objections to the recommended award.

findings.title: Technical scoring criteria and breakdown
findings.fact: The RFP does not provide a detailed breakdown of technical scoring criteria or weights for evaluation factors.

quotes.quote: V. PROPOSAL EVALUATION

findings.title: Financial Scoring Formula
findings.fact: Cost Effectiveness is one of the evaluation criteria with a weight of 15 points, but no specific formula is provided.

quotes.quote: 5 Cost Effectiveness 15

findings.title: Fully loaded hourly rate definition
findings.fact: Fully loaded hourly rate includes all applicable surcharges such as taxes, insurance, fringe benefits, indirect costs, overhead, profit allowance, and ordinary materials and supplies.

quotes.quote: fully loaded hourly rate means an hourly rate that includes all applicable surcharges such as taxes, insurance and fringe benefits as well as indirect costs, overhead and profit allowance, and ordinary materials and supplies.

findings.title: Monthly invoices required
findings.fact: The consultant shall submit monthly invoices and progress reports as part of Task 1 deliverables.

quotes.quote: Monthly Invoices and Progress reports

findings.title: Cost proposal required with detailed task-based breakdown
findings.fact: The cost proposal must be task-based, including personnel names, classifications, hourly rates, and other cost items, with a total cost summary.

quotes.quote: Provide a detailed task-based cost proposal for the project using the Cost Proposal Template (Appendix C). The cost estimate shall include personnel names, classifications, hourly rates, and any other cost items necessary to perform each of the tasks listed in the Scope of Work. A total cost shall be summarized and presented.

findings.title: Cost effectiveness evaluation criteria
findings.fact: Cost effectiveness is an evaluation criterion with a weight of 15 points, assessing cost control, budgeting methodology, clarity of cost in spreadsheet format, reasonableness of hourly rates, and resource allocation.

quotes.quote: 5. Cost Effectiveness (15 points) • Cost Control and Budgeting Methodology o Proposer has a system or process for managing cost and budget. o Evidence of successful budget management for a similar project. • Proposal clearly defines cost in spreadsheet format. • Reasonableness of hourly rates. • Allocation of resources for tasks and activities.

findings.title: Minimum Qualifications: Three Similar Projects in Past Ten Years
findings.fact: Proposer must demonstrate successful completion of at least three projects in the past ten years related to Local Roadway Safety Plan, Systemic Safety Analysis Report (SSAR), Vision Zero Action Plan, and/or supplemental or implementation planning for the Safe Streets for All Grant Program.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must have a strong track record in safety planning projects to be considered. Lack of such experience will result in disqualification.
findings.action_recommendation: Review team qualifications and ensure the prime or subconsultants collectively have at least three relevant projects completed in the last ten years. Prepare detailed project descriptions and references to demonstrate compliance.

quotes.quote: Proposer must demonstrate to C/CAG’s satisfaction that the prime consultant and/or one or more subconsultant proposed this project have successfully completed at least three (3) projects in the past ten (10) years related to Local Roadway Safety Plan, Systemic Safety Analysis Report (SSAR), Vision Zero Action Plan and/or supplemental or implementation planning for the Safe Streets for All Grant Program.

findings.title: Experience with Federal Grant Funded Projects
findings.fact: Proposers must demonstrate experience managing and implementing large-scale federal grant funded projects and ensuring compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local requirements.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must prove capability to handle federal grants, including compliance with complex regulations. This is critical for project success and avoiding legal issues.
findings.action_recommendation: Highlight past federal grant projects in the proposal, emphasizing compliance management. Provide examples of successful audits and adherence to federal requirements.

quotes.quote: Proposers must demonstrate experience managing and implementing large-scale federal grant funded projects and successfully ensuring compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local requirements for such projects.

findings.title: Pre-qualification Criteria
findings.fact: Proposals must comply with RFP requirements; incomplete submittals will be deemed non-responsive and disqualified.
findings.business_implication: Any missing or incorrect information in the proposal can lead to immediate disqualification, regardless of technical merit.
findings.action_recommendation: Create a compliance checklist based on the RFP and conduct a thorough review before submission. Ensure all required forms, signatures, and attachments are included.

quotes.quote: An initial assessment will be made to ensure that the submittal complies with the RFP requirements. An incomplete submittal will be deemed non-responsive and disqualified at C/CAG staff’s discretion.

findings.title: Final Bid Submission Deadline
findings.fact: Proposals must be received by C/CAG no later than 12 PM PST on Friday, January 23, 2026.
findings.business_implication: Missing the deadline will result in rejection. Timely submission is critical to be considered.
findings.action_recommendation: Plan submission well in advance, allowing for technical issues. Submit early to avoid last-minute problems. Confirm receipt with the contact person.

quotes.quote: Proposals are due: January 23, 2026, 12:00PM PST
Proposals must be received by C/CAG no later than 12 PM PST on Friday, January 23, 2026, in accordance with the instructions contained in the RFP.

findings.title: Q&A / Clarification Deadline
findings.fact: Deadline for Requests for Clarifications is January 9, 2026.
findings.business_implication: Clarifications must be submitted by this date to ensure understanding of requirements and avoid misinterpretation.
findings.action_recommendation: Review the RFP thoroughly and submit any questions by January 9, 2026. Monitor C/CAG website for addenda and incorporate into proposal.

quotes.quote: Deadline for Requests for Clarifications: January 9, 2026
Friday, January 9, 2026 Question and Answer Deadline

findings.title: Bid Validity Period
findings.fact: Proposal must be a firm offer for 120 days from the due date for proposals.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must commit to holding its proposed pricing and terms for 120 days, which may expose it to cost increases or resource availability risks during that period.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure internal approval for a 120-day validity period and include contingency plans for potential cost fluctuations.

quotes.quote: Indicate that the proposal is a firm offer to enter into a contract to perform work related to this RFP for a period of 120 days from the due date for proposals.

findings.title: Formatting and Envelope Rules
findings.fact: Proposals must be submitted electronically in PDF format, with specific page size, numbering, and page limit requirements.
findings.business_implication: Non-compliance with formatting requirements could lead to disqualification or a lower evaluation score, jeopardizing the bid.
findings.action_recommendation: Carefully format the proposal according to the specified page size, numbering, and page limit, and double-check before submission.

quotes.quote: Consultants must submit one (1) electronic copy of the proposal in pdf format. Each page shall be 8.5” x 11” or 11” x 17”. Each page shall be sequentially numbered, and a table of contents shall be provided. Each submittal shall be no more than 20 pages, excluding cover letter, title page, table of contents, resumes of key staff members, relevant experience, and references.

findings.title: Portal Upload Instructions
findings.fact: Proposals should be emailed with the subject line 'RFP – San Mateo Countywide Safe Streets for All Supplemental Planning Project' to Eva Gaye (egaye@smcgov.org).
findings.business_implication: Failure to follow the submission instructions exactly could result in the proposal being overlooked or rejected.
findings.action_recommendation: Use the exact subject line and send the proposal to the specified email address before the deadline.

quotes.quote: Proposals should be emailed with the subject line “RFP – San Mateo Countywide Safe Streets for All Supplemental Planning Project” to: Eva Gaye (egaye@smcgov.org).

findings.title: Disqualification conditions
findings.fact: Proposals received after the deadline may be considered nonresponsive; unsigned proposals or proposals signed by unauthorized individuals will be rejected.
findings.business_implication: Late or improperly signed proposals will be rejected, wasting the bidder's time and resources.
findings.action_recommendation: Submit the proposal well before the deadline and ensure it is signed by an authorized representative.

quotes.quote: Proposals received after the time and date specified above may be considered nonresponsive.
Unsigned proposals or proposals signed by an individual not authorized to bind the prospective consultant will be considered nonresponsive and rejected.

findings.title: Evaluation Criteria and Weights
findings.fact: Proposals are evaluated on written criteria (80 points) and interview criteria (20 points) with specific weights for each criterion.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must prioritize the highest-weighted criteria (Staff and Firm Qualifications, Understanding of Project Scope, and Proposed Project Approach) to maximize its score.
findings.action_recommendation: Allocate proposal development effort according to the weights, ensuring strong content in the key areas and preparing thoroughly for the interview.

quotes.quote: No. Written Evaluation Criteria Weight 1 Organization of Proposal 5 2 Staff and Firm Qualifications 20 3 Understanding of Project Scope of Work 20 4 Proposed Project Approach 15 5 Cost Effectiveness 15 6 References 5 7 Conflict of Interest Statement Pass/Fail Subtotal: 80
No. Interview Evaluation Criteria Weight 8 Presentation by team 10 9 Q&A Response to panel questions 10 Subtotal: 20 Total: 100

findings.title: Minimum Qualifying Technical Threshold
findings.fact: A score of 0 on any mandatory requirement results in disqualification.
findings.business_implication: Any mandatory requirement scored as 0 will lead to automatic disqualification, regardless of overall score. This underscores the critical importance of fully addressing all mandatory requirements in the proposal.
findings.action_recommendation: Conduct a thorough review of the RFP to identify all mandatory requirements. Ensure each is explicitly and convincingly addressed in the proposal to avoid any risk of a 0 score. Consider having a compliance checklist and internal review process.

quotes.quote: 0 Not Acceptable Non-responsive, fails to meet RFP specifications. The approach has no probability of success. For mandatory requirement this score will result in disqualification of proposal.

findings.title: Disqualification Conditions
findings.fact: Incomplete submittals are deemed non-responsive and disqualified at C/CAG staff's discretion. Contacting evaluators may also risk disqualification.
findings.business_implication: Submitting an incomplete proposal or contacting evaluators during the evaluation process can lead to disqualification at C/CAG's discretion. This introduces significant risk that could be avoided by careful compliance.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure the proposal is complete and all required documents are included. Strictly adhere to the communication protocol by directing all inquiries to the C/CAG Contract Administrator/Project Manager only. Avoid any direct or indirect contact with evaluation committee members.

quotes.quote: An incomplete submittal will be deemed non-responsive and disqualified at C/CAG staff’s discretion.
Attempts by proposer to contact members of the Committee may jeopardize the integrity of the evaluation and selection process and risk possible disqualification of proposer.

findings.title: Indemnification for Public Records Act Release
findings.fact: Proposers agree to indemnify and hold harmless C/CAG for release of information under the Public Records Act.
findings.business_implication: By submitting a proposal, the bidder consents to the release of all submitted materials under the Public Records Act and agrees to indemnify C/CAG for any release. This could expose the bidder to liability if confidential or proprietary information is released.
findings.action_recommendation: Before submitting, carefully review all materials for any confidential or proprietary information. Consider marking sensitive information and understand that it may still be subject to disclosure. Evaluate the potential risks and ensure that the indemnification obligation is acceptable. If necessary, consult legal counsel.

quotes.quote: By submitting materials, (1) you consent to release of such materials by C/CAG if requested under the Public Records Act without further notice to you, and (2) you agree to indemnify and hold harmless C/CAG for release of such information.

findings.title: Termination for Conflict of Interest
findings.fact: C/CAG may terminate the contract if a conflict of interest is discovered and not resolved.
findings.business_implication: If a conflict of interest is discovered during the contract and not resolved, C/CAG can terminate the contract. This could lead to loss of revenue and potential reputational damage.
findings.action_recommendation: Proactively identify and disclose any potential conflicts of interest in the proposal. Establish a process to monitor for conflicts during the contract and promptly notify C/CAG if any arise. Work with C/CAG to resolve conflicts in a timely manner to avoid termination.

quotes.quote: The C/CAG Project Manager may terminate the contract involving the conflict of interest and C/CAG may obtain the conflicted services in any way allowed by law.

findings.title: Termination for Cause for Failure to Notify Conflict
findings.fact: Failure to notify C/CAG of a conflict of interest may be grounds for termination for cause.
findings.business_implication: If the bidder fails to notify C/CAG of a conflict of interest, the contract may be terminated for cause, which could have negative consequences for the bidder's reputation and future opportunities.
findings.action_recommendation: Implement a robust conflict of interest identification and reporting mechanism. Ensure all team members are aware of the obligation to disclose conflicts immediately. If a conflict arises, notify the C/CAG Project Manager in writing as soon as possible.

quotes.quote: Failure by the consultant to notify C/CAG Project Manager may be grounds for termination of the contract for cause pursuant to Section 4, Termination, of the Contract Agreement Template, provided as Appendix D to this RFP.

findings.title: Termination for Material Breach for Key Personnel Changes
findings.fact: Removal of key personnel without prior written consent may be considered a material breach of contract, potentially leading to termination.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must ensure that any changes to key personnel during the contract require prior written consent from C/CAG. Failure to do so could result in termination of the contract, leading to financial loss and reputational damage.
findings.action_recommendation: The bidder should establish an internal process to obtain C/CAG's written approval before making any changes to key personnel. This includes identifying key personnel in the proposal and ensuring they are committed for the project duration. If changes are unavoidable, the bidder should proactively communicate with C/CAG and seek approval in advance.

quotes.quote: Removal of any key personnel identified in the responses to the RFP without prior written consent of C/CAG may be considered a material breach of contract.

findings.title: C/CAG Right to Cancel RFP
findings.fact: C/CAG reserves the right to modify or cancel the RFP in part or in its entirety if in its best interests.
findings.business_implication: C/CAG can cancel the RFP at any time, which means the bidder may incur costs in preparing the proposal without any guarantee of contract award. This introduces uncertainty and potential financial risk.
findings.action_recommendation: The bidder should carefully consider the costs of proposal preparation and ensure they are not excessive. They should also monitor any updates or addenda to the RFP and be prepared for possible cancellation. It is advisable to maintain flexibility and avoid making significant commitments based solely on this RFP.

quotes.quote: C/CAG reserves the right to accept or reject all proposals submitted, waive minor irregularities, request additional information, negotiate with any qualified consultant, or modify or cancel in part or in its entirety the RFP if it is in the best interests of C/CAG to do so.

findings.title: Termination for Failure to Enter Contract
findings.fact: If the selected proposer fails to enter into a contract in a timely manner, C/CAG may reject the proposal and contract with the next highest scoring proposer.
findings.business_implication: If the bidder is selected but fails to sign the contract promptly, they risk losing the award to the next highest scorer. This could result in lost business opportunity and wasted effort.
findings.action_recommendation: The bidder should be prepared to enter into the contract immediately upon selection. They should have all necessary approvals and resources in place to execute the contract without delay. It is also important to review the contract terms in advance to avoid any surprises that could cause delays.

quotes.quote: If the selected proposer fails to enter into a contract with C/CAG in a timely manner as determined by C/CAG, C/CAG reserves the right to reject the proposal and enter into a contract with the next highest scoring proposer.

findings.title: Conflicting Evaluation Criteria Weights
findings.fact: The evaluation criteria summary lists weights that sum to 80 for written criteria and 20 for interview criteria, totaling 100. However, the weighted score table shows a total of 100/500, which is inconsistent with the stated maximum score of 500 points.
findings.business_implication: The inconsistency in the evaluation scoring may lead to confusion about how proposals will be scored. The bidder may not know the actual maximum score or how to optimize their proposal to maximize points. This could affect their competitive strategy.
findings.action_recommendation: The bidder should seek clarification from C/CAG regarding the evaluation scoring methodology. They should ask for a clear explanation of how the weights translate to the 500-point scale and how the total score will be calculated. This will help the bidder understand the evaluation process and tailor their proposal accordingly.
